findings.passage: State Rep. Bob Morris (R-Fort Wayne) said to register, Indiana residents must be at least 18 years old on or before the upcoming election, have a valid Indiana Driver's License or Indiana State Identification Card, be a citizen of the United States, have lived in the same precinct for at least 30 days before the next election, and not currently imprisoned after being convicted of a crime.
findings.note: Joint press release from Allen County House members. Describes current registration requirements (state ID or driver's license, citizenship) as attributed to Morris in indirect speech. Describes existing law; does not say he wants it changed.

findings.passage: "IndianaVoters.com provides a simple way to register and it takes just a few minutes," Morris said.
findings.note: Joint press release. Morris encourages online registration and checking eligibility. The same release lists the ID and citizenship rules for registering, but attributes that sentence to another member. No view on voter ID itself.

findings.motion: SB 10 - Culp - 3rd Reading: Bill Passed (roll call 340)
findings.note: IN House, SB 10 - Culp - 3rd Reading: Bill Passed (roll call 340), 2025-04-01: yea (tally 66–26); census gate: none.

findings.passage: “For those who hold certain religious beliefs against having their photograph taken, they have been unable to make use of those services because of the law. That is why I am proud to author this legislation that not only addresses this issue, but prevents against false information from being submitted as well.”
findings.note: Press release quoting him on his bill to let people with a religious objection to photos get a state non-photo ID. The release says the card does not allow the holder to vote.

findings.motion: HB 1631 (2015), state photo-exempt ID for religious objectors; passed the Senate 37-13
findings.note: He authored the bill. The Bureau of Motor Vehicles would issue a photo-exempt ID to U.S. citizens with a religious objection to being photographed. The release says the bill does not allow the holder to vote, and makes false information on the ID a felony. The release gives the number as HB 1631 in one place and HB 1361 in another.
